question: Which of the following two states have jointly conducted a Nilgiri Tahr census in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nilgiri Tahr Census:** The **Nilgiri Tahr census** is a joint initiative conducted by the states of **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu** in **April 2025**. The primary objective is to estimate the population and study the distribution of the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered species endemic to the **Western Ghats**.
 
• **Collaboration:** Both states collaborated in **April 2025** to undertake a comprehensive survey of the species. This effort highlights their commitment to preserving biodiversity in the ecologically sensitive **Western Ghats**.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** The **Nilgiri Tahr** is classified as **Endangered** under the **IUCN Red List** due to habitat loss and declining population. The census is essential for evaluating existing conservation measures and developing future strategies.
 
• **Habitat:** The species is predominantly found in the **Nilgiri Hills** and other parts of the **Western Ghats**, which span across **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu**. These regions are known for their rich biodiversity and unique ecosystems.
 
• **Protected Areas:** Conservation efforts include protected areas like **Eravikulam National Park** in Kerala and **Mukurthi National Park** in Tamil Nadu, which are critical habitats for the **Nilgiri Tahr**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nilgiri Tahr:**

 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is a mountain goat-like ungulate species endemic to the **Western Ghats** of India.
 
• **Scientific Name:** *Nilgiritragus hylocrius*.
 
• It is the **state animal** of Tamil Nadu and primarily inhabits high-altitude **grasslands** and rocky areas.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Status:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is classified as **Endangered** under the **IUCN Red List**, with major threats including habitat destruction, poaching, and livestock competition.
 
 
 
• **Key Protected Areas:**
 
 
• **Eravikulam National Park:** Located in Kerala, this park hosts the **largest population** of Nilgiri Tahr.
 
• **Mukurthi National Park:** Situated in Tamil Nadu, it is another critical habitat for the species.
 
• **Silent Valley National Park:** Located in Kerala, contributing significantly to biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr Recovery Program** was launched to monitor and protect the species.
 
• Regular **censuses** and **habitat restoration initiatives** are being carried out by both state governments.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The **Western Ghats** is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known for its exceptional biodiversity and is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity globally.
 
• It spans across six Indian states: **Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, and Gujarat**.
 
• It is the origin of many perennial rivers such as **Godavari, Kaveri, and Krishna**, essential for agriculture and drinking water.
 
• Threats include **deforestation**, **climate change**, and **human encroachment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Importance of Biodiversity Conservation:**

 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr census** is a vital step towards understanding and conserving endangered species in the **Western Ghats**.
 
• Efforts like afforestation, strict wildlife protection laws, and the establishment of protected areas are essential to mitigate biodiversity loss.
 
 
 
• **Role of State Collaboration:**
 
 
• The collaboration between **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu** showcases the importance of joint efforts in addressing ecological challenges.
